newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac's popularity dips, Juppe's stagnates--poll.
newsitem.headline: Chirac's popularity dips, Juppe's stagnates--poll.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac's popularity dipped in March and Prime Minister Alain Juppe's rating stagnated, halting a gradual rise for both conservative leaders this year, an opinion poll showed on Saturday.

The IFOP survey, for the weekly Journal du Dimanche, showed that just 32 percent of those questioned were satisfied with Chirac as president, down from 34 percent in February. The number of those dissatisfied was flat at 55 percent.
Juppe's popularity rating was unchanged at 29 percent while the percentage of those dissatisfied dipped to 60 percent from 61 in the survey of 1,833 people from March 13 to 21.

Both Chirac and Juppe's ratings had steadily crept up from lows in November 1995, when just 27 percent were satisfied with Chirac and just 20 percent with Juppe. Juppe has borne the brunt of blame for high unemployment in France.
